INSTRUCTIONS FOR PREPARING A

MAGISTRATE’S DECISION

All Magistrate’s Decisions shall be titled “MAGISTRATE’S DECISION”. Include the name of the Common Pleas judge assigned to the case in the caption.

The Magistrate’s Decision shall provide the following statement:

Objections to the Magistrate’s Decision must be filed within fourteen days of the filing date of the Magistrate’s Decision. A party shall not assign as error on appeal the court’s adoption of any factual finding or legal conclusion, whether or not specifically designated as a finding of fact or conclusion of law under Civ. R. 53(D)(3)(a)(ii), unless the party timely and specifically objects to that factual finding or legal conclusion as required by Civ. R. 53(D)(3)(b).”

All Magistrate’s Decisions shall be accompanied by a “Praecipe” which identifies all parties or their counsel for service by the Clerk. The praecipe may be included in the body of the document after the signature block and after the required Notice quoted above. A blank praecipe may be obtained from the Magistrate’s staff.

The “Certificate of Service” shall read:

“I hereby certify that copies of the foregoing decision have been sent by ordinary mail to all parties or their attorneys as provided above.

Date: Deputy Clerk: ”

The Magistrate’s Decision shall be presented to the Magistrate’s courtroom (Room 585).

If no objections are filed within 14 days (see Sipes v. Martini 1st Dist. Hamilton No. C-100025, 2010-Ohio-4598), counsel shall prepare a judgment entry adopting the Magistrate’s Decision and submit same to the Magistrate’s courtroom.

A model Magistrate’s Decision and Entry Adopting Magistrate’s Decision are included herein for review.

COURT OF COMMON PLEAS

HAMILTON COUNTY, OHIO

YYYYYYYYYYYYY, : Case No. Axxxxxxx

Plaintiff, : Judge xxxxx

MAGISTRATE’S DECISION

Defendant(s). :

RENDERED THIS \_\_\_\_\_\_ DAY OF MONTH, 20xx.

Place operative facts here.

ANITA P. BERDING,

COURT OF COMMON PLEAS

Objections to the Magistrate’s Decision must be filed within fourteen days of the filing date of the Magistrate’s Decision. A party shall not assign as error on appeal the court’s adoption of any factual finding or legal conclusion, whether or not specifically designated as a finding of fact or conclusion of law under Civ. R. 53(D)(3)(a)(ii), unless the party timely and specifically objects to that factual finding or legal conclusion as required by Civ. R. 53(D)(3)(b).

Copies sent by Clerk of Courts to:

Jane A. Attorney, Esq. Bill C. Homeowner, Esq.

Plaintiff Law Firm Defendant Law Firm

100 Main Street 100 Sycamore Street

Cincinnati, Ohio 45202 Cincinnati, Ohio 45202

CERTIFICATE OF SERVICE

I HEREBY CERTIFY THAT COPIES OF THE FOREGOING DECISION HAVE BEEN SENT BY ORDINARY MAIL TO ALL PARTIES OR THEIR ATTORNEYS AS PROVIDED ABOVE.

Date: Deputy Clerk:

COURT OF COMMON PLEAS

HAMILTON COUNTY, OHIO

XXXXXXXXXXX, et al., : Case No. A1XXXXXX

Plaintiff, : Judge XXXX

ENTRY ADOPTING

YYYYYYYYYYY, et al., : MAGISTRATE’S DECISION

Defendants. :

Pursuant to Civil Rule 53, the Court hereby adopts the Magistrate’s Decision rendered on \[DATE.\] The objection period has expired with no objections having been filed and no extensions having been granted. The Magistrate’s Decision is ADOPTED as a judgment of the court.

\[Place Finding of Decision here, such as…\] Plaintiff’s Motion for Summary Judgment filed January 1, 2013 is GRANTED.

COURT OF COMMON PLEAS
